title: A pure substance
competency: Use the particle theory to tell pure substances from mixtures.

keywords.def: A single kind of matter that cannot be separated into other kinds by physical means.
A physical combination of two or more substances.

en.text: Matter can be classified as pure substances or mixtures. A pure substance is a single kind of matter. It has a definite, constant composition and cannot be separated by physical means. Pure water, oxygen, gold, sugar and table salt are pure substances. Pure substances are elements or compounds.

screens.title: Just one thing
screens.ask: Which one is "only one substance and nothing else"?
screens.after: Pure water is water and nothing else. The others contain several substances: they are mixtures.

screens.title: 2.3 Classification of substances
paras: Matter can also be classified by its chemical composition.
There are two classes: pure substances and mixtures.

root.label: Matter
root.info: Anything that has mass and occupies space.

children.label: Element
children.info: Cannot be broken down into simpler substances.

children.label: Compound
children.info: Can be broken down into its elements by chemical, not physical, means.

children.label: Mixture
children.info: Physical combination of two or more substances.

screens.title: 2.3.1 A pure substance
paras: A pure substance is a single kind of matter.
It cannot be separated into other kinds of matter by physical means.
Pure water is water and nothing else.
A pure substance has a definite and constant composition.
Examples: oxygen, sulfur, copper, silver, gold, sugar, table salt, water, carbon dioxide.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A single kind of matter that cannot be separated into other kinds by physical means.
A physical combination of two or more substances.

screens.text: Pure substance: which one is a pure substance?
screens.why:
A pure substance is one kind of matter with a fixed composition.
Air is several gases. Milk is water, fat and protein. Soil is many things.
Table salt is one substance only.
Answer: table salt.
screens.clue: Which one is only one substance?

screens.why:
Ask: is it one substance, or several mixed together?
Iron and oxygen are elements; sugar is a compound: pure substances.
Sugar solution (sugar + water), milk and air contain several substances: mixtures.
screens.clue: Is it one substance, or several?
screens.text: Sort each one: pure substance or mixture?
True or false: a pure substance can be separated into other substances by sieving or filtering.
screens.why:
Sieving and filtering are physical means.
A pure substance is a single kind of matter.
It cannot be separated by physical means.
So the statement is false.

screens.text: Pure or mixture: pure water and a salt solution both look clear. What is the difference?
opts: Salt solution is a mixture; salt can be separated by evaporation
screens.ans: Salt solution is a mixture; salt can be separated by evaporation
screens.why:
Pure water: one substance with a fixed composition.
Salt solution: salt + water, two substances.
Let the water evaporate and the salt is left behind.
So the salt solution is a mixture that can be separated by a physical method.
screens.clue: Can you get anything out of each by a physical method?

test.text: Classification by composition: matter is classified into …
test.why:
By chemical composition there are two classes.
Pure substances have one kind of matter; mixtures have two or more.
Solid and liquid are states, not composition classes.
Answer: pure substances and mixtures.

test.text: True or false: a pure substance always has a definite and constant composition.
test.why:
A pure substance is one kind of matter.
Pure water is always water and nothing else.
So its composition never changes.
The statement is true.

test.text: Figure 2.6: pure substances are further classified as …
test.why:
Figure 2.6 splits pure substances into two groups.
Elements cannot be broken down into simpler substances.
Compounds can be broken down into elements by chemical means.
Answer: elements and compounds.

test.text: Pure substance or mixture: which one is NOT a pure substance?
test.why:
Gold is an element. Carbon dioxide and sugar are compounds.
Ink is dyes dissolved in alcohol and water.
That is several substances mixed: a mixture.
Answer: ink.

test.text: Composition (Review Exercise): which one has a variable composition?
test.why:
Pure substances have a fixed composition: water, salt, silver.
Milk is a mixture of water, fat, protein and sugar.
The amounts can differ from one milk to another.
Answer: milk.
